The region is defined by ancient Amani troll temple ruins, the towering aeries of the Wildhammer clan at Aerie Peak, and a colossal Great Tree anchoring a mysterious rift to the Emerald Dream. Long before humans or dwarves walked northern Lordaeron, the forest trolls of the Amani Empire held dominion over the Hinterlands. Following their defeat in the ancient Troll Wars, their empire shattered into disparate tribes. Centuries later, after the tragic War of the Three Hammers drove the Wildhammer dwarves from Grim Batol, the dwarves migrated north and made their home on the surface at Aerie Peak. Taming the native gryphons and embracing shamanic traditions, the Wildhammer constructed a massive skybound stronghold. The trolls viewed these surface-dwelling dwarves as unwelcome squatters upon ancestral lands, sparking a ceaseless feud of skirmishes and raids. Three distinct forest troll factions occupy the dense canopy and crumbling stone temples. The brutal and fanatical Vilebranch tribe is the strongest, maintaining sprawling strongholds at the terraced temple-city of Jintha'Alor and the towering Altar of Zul. To the south, the weaker Witherbark tribe clings to Shadra'Alor and Hiri'Watha. The nomadic Revantusk tribe, long scorned by their cousins and lacking a true home, chose a radical path after the Third War: they struck a treaty with Thrall's New Horde. Bolstered by orcish and Forsaken aid, the Revantusk founded Revantusk Village on the eastern sea cliffs, carving out a defiant coastal bastion.

zone:lochmodan.text: Loch Modan. Loch Modan is a temperate mountain valley east of Dun Morogh, renowned for its massive alpine lake held in place by the monumental Stonewrought Dam. Centered around the dwarven town of Thelsamar, the region struggles under encroaching trogg infestations, kobolds in the mines, and aggressive ogres in the northeast highlands. Situated in eastern Khaz Modan, Loch Modan presents a stark, pleasant contrast to the frozen snowfields of Dun Morogh. Rugged mountain peaks enclose a temperate valley of pine and birch, cradling the Loch itself. This massive body of fresh water is held in place by the Stonewrought Dam, an architectural triumph that towers along the northern rim. The peaceful settlement of Thelsamar serves as the civic heart of the territory, housing traveling mountaineers, hunters, and miners who ply the productive veins of copper and tin scattered throughout the hills. Loch Modan's tranquil scenery conceals recurrent violence. Broken catapults and ballistae resting on the lake bed remain from the Second War, when the orcish Horde occupied the valley before the dwarves drove them out. More recently, dwarven archaeological excavations accidentally unearthed subterranean swarms of savage troggs. Led by savage chieftains, trogg tribes have overrun the southern canyons of Stonesplinter Valley and the Valley of Kings, threatening trade routes and forcing the Ironforge Mountaineers to wage a desperate defense.

zone:mulgore.text: Mulgore. Mulgore is the ancestral homeland of the tauren, a lush, sheltered valley of emerald grasslands, towering plateaus, and rolling plains nestled beneath the Stonetalon Mountains. Surrounded by high natural mountain walls, the realm was secured after Cairne Bloodhoof allied with Thrall's Horde to drive out the marauding centaur. Today, it serves as the spiritual and territorial heartland of the united tauren tribes, overseen from the great mesa city of Thunder Bluff. For generations, the tauren lived as nomads, perpetually hunted and displaced across the central plains by aggressive centaur warbands. Their fortune shifted when High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof encountered Thrall and his displaced orcs. Recognizing shared ideals of honor, shamanism, and strength, the tauren forged an alliance with the nascent Horde. With orcish assistance, Cairne broke the centaur's grip on the region and led his people into Mulgore. Here, they built permanent settlements for the first time in centuries, crowning the highest northern mesas with their capital, Thunder Bluff. Reaching maturity in Mulgore requires answering the call of the Great Hunt and honoring the Earthmother. Young tauren begin their training on the southern plateau of Red Cloud Mesa at Camp Narache under Chief Hawkwind. As they descend into the Golden Plains and Bloodhoof Village, they undertake the Rites of the Earthmother, learning to commune with ancestral spirits, forage native herbs, and respect the herds of kodos and tallstriders that sustain their civilization. Despite its tranquil appearance, Mulgore faces growing threats from all quarters. Displaced quilboar have entrenched themselves within Brambleblade Ravine and defiled the sacred burial grounds of Red Rocks. In the mountains, Windfury harpies prey upon wild game, while Palemane gnolls strike from hidden caves. More troubling still are external exploitations: the commercial goblins of the Venture Company have begun defiling the sacred water wells and quarrying the eastern hills, while dwarven explorers from Bael Modan have established the Bael'dun Digsite to unearth ancient titan artifacts against tauren protests.

zone:orgrimmar.text: Orgrimmar. Orgrimmar is the fortress capital of the orcs and the beating heart of Thrall's New Horde. Carved directly into the towering red-rock canyons of northern Durotar, the fortified city stands as a monument to orcish perseverance and an unyielding sanctuary for trolls, tauren, and Forsaken allies alike. Following the Third War, Warchief Thrall led the orcs to the arid coasts of Kalimdor to build a homeland free from demonic corruption and human bondage. Naming the harsh region Durotar after his father, Thrall established Orgrimmar in memory of his fallen mentor, Orgrim Doomhammer. Raising the city required blood and sweat; aided by the tauren, the Darkspear trolls, goblin engineers, and the Champion Rexxar, the Horde drove back encroaching centaur, harpies, and ferocious thunder lizards to secure the canyon stronghold. Orgrimmar is naturally fortified by rugged mountains that shield it from both foreign invaders and the violent razor-winds sweeping through Durotar. The settlement is partitioned into distinct natural hollows. The Valley of Strength serves as the bustling civic gatehouse, leading deeper into the trade bazaar of The Drag. Tauren druids and shaman congregate in the serene pools of the Valley of Wisdom, while Darkspear shadow hunters and witch doctors dwell among the stilted pavilions of the Valley of Spirits.

zone:ragefire.text: Ragefire Chasm. Ragefire Chasm is a network of winding volcanic tunnels situated directly beneath the orcish capital of Orgrimmar. Entered through the dark hollows of the Cleft of Shadow, the chasm is overrun by savage troggs and a demonic sect of cultists known as the Searing Blade. Left unchecked, the dark powers and subterranean swarms festering below threaten the very foundation of the young Horde nation. Beneath the dust and red rocks of Orgrimmar lies a blistering maze of volcanic corridors and lava pits. While orcish builders forged their new home above, aggressive Ragefire troggs began erupting from deep below the surface. Magatha Grimtotem sought to open diplomatic channels with the brutes on behalf of Thunder Bluff, but her envoy Maur Grimtotem was slaughtered, proving the troggs will yield only to force. Far more dangerous than simple troggs is the presence of the Searing Blade, a fanatical cell loyal to the Shadow Council. Operating from the dark caverns alongside the magma streams, this demonic cult plots the utter ruin of the fledgling Horde. They are led by the warlock Jergosh the Invoker, a cunning satyr named Bazzalan, and the vicious felguard Taragaman the Hungerer, who presides over an altar in the lava lake.

zone:redridge.text: Redridge Mountains. East of Elwynn Forest, the Redridge Mountains feature rushing rivers, wooded slopes, and the serene expanse of Lake Everstill. Despite its scenic heights, the region is besieged by hostile Shadowhide gnolls and the encroaching Blackrock orcs of the Dark Horde. With the kingdom's military tied up by internal strife in Stormwind, the lakeside town of Lakeshire must rely on wandering mercenaries to hold the line. The Redridge range was once among the most peaceful corners of the kingdom, supplying Stormwind with timber, freshwater fish, and crops. Today, that quiet life has eroded. The lakeside township of Lakeshire sits perpetually fortified against aggressive incursions. To the east, Stonewatch Keep—once a proud bastion of the kingdom—has fallen under the control of renegade Blackrock orcs, cutting off roads and threatening to overrun the eastern valleys entirely. Geographically, these peaks form part of the spine running down the subcontinent of Azeroth. Centuries ago, the mountain chain reached much farther north until the Dark Iron clan inadvertently summoned the Firelord Ragnaros, tearing the earth asunder and creating the fiery crater of Blackrock Mountain. That cataclysm severed the northern peaks into the ash-choked Burning Steppes, leaving only the southern Redridge valleys lush, green, and vulnerable to attacks descending from the slopes above. While Magistrate Solomon and Marshal Marris plead for reinforcements, the regency council in Stormwind has effectively abandoned Lakeshire to fend for itself. Desperate entreaties sent to Sentinel Hill and Darkshire yield nothing, as both sister settlements are crippled by their own crises. With reinforcements nowhere in sight, local magistrates must hire any capable sellsword willing to brave the Lakeridge Highway, clear the gnoll camps, and push back the shadow looming over Lake Everstill.

zone:riverglades.text: Riverglades. The Riverglades is a contested river valley east of the Burning Steppes and Badlands, historically claimed by the Kingdom of Stormwind. Overrun by the Old Horde during the First War and largely abandoned by the crown, the region remains a battleground as local human loyalists clash with modern Horde outposts and local wildlife. It borders Redridge Mountains to the southwest, Swamp of Sorrows to the south, and faces Tanaris across the sea. Historically part of the Kingdom of Stormwind, the Riverglades fell into ruin during the First War when the Old Horde swept through the region. Its central settlement, Sunnyglade, was sacked by the orcs, who spared its mage tower solely to study human sorcery before enslaving the surviving townsfolk. Though Stormwind soldiers mounted an effort to liberate the captives and rebuild, the kingdom eventually deemed the entire valley lost and diverted resources toward defending the core homelands. For years, the region remained largely cut off from formal crown support. Despite being left behind by Stormwind's higher leadership, the human defenders never fully surrendered their homeland. Under Knight Commander Demar Brant of the legendary Brotherhood of the Horse, the remaining loyalists hold Farholde Keep as a bastion against the wilderness and hostile invaders. Meanwhile, the modern Horde maintains their own strong presence nearby at outposts like Rog'mar and Bolder'ok, ensuring that the ancient conflict over the glades continues to smolder. Stretching along the coast of the Forbidding Sea, the Riverglades is flanked by mountainous terrain and winding waterways. Travelers on foot can cross west through Blackrock Pass to the Burning Steppes, wind southwest through Redridge Pass toward the Redridge Mountains, navigate south into the Swamp of Sorrows, or trek northwest past Twilight's Shroud into the Badlands. On the coast, Powderfuse Port provides sea passage connecting directly across the ocean to Steamwheedle Port in Tanaris.

zone:ruinsoflordaeron.text: Ruins of Lordaeron. Perched directly above the subterranean Undercity, the Ruins of Lordaeron are the hollow remains of humanity's once-mighty northern kingdom. Fallen to the Scourge and Prince Arthas during the Third War, the surface streets and cracked plazas now crawl with wandering monstrosities, vengeful specters, and vile experimenters. Both the Alliance and the Horde dispatch ventures into this blighted citadel to reclaim relics of the fallen past or purge the horrors lurking above the Forsaken capital. Capital City was once the crown jewel of the Eastern Kingdoms, the seat of King Terenas Menethil II and the beating heart of human civilization. When Prince Arthas returned from Northrend, he slew his father in the throne room and unleashed the undead upon the citizenry. Today, while the Forsaken dwell in the catacombs of the Undercity below, the surface ruins remain a forsaken twilight zone. Broken archways and weed-choked cobbles shelter feral beasts like Witherfang and deranged remnants of the past. The dangers within the ruined grounds go beyond restless dead. Apothecaries and sinister figures like Viktor the Vile work on testing new plagues among the shadows, while twisted experiments like The Abandoned roam freely. Wrathful spirits such as Rath'mael and cursed retainers like The Baron haunt the collapsed hallways, locked in unending torment and striking out against any living or undead trespassers who cross their paths.

zone:searinggorge.text: Searing Gorge. Searing Gorge is a scorched, desolate canyon in southern Khaz Modan, bordering Blackrock Mountain to the south. Once a verdant expanse of the Redridge Mountains, it was devastated over two centuries ago by the apocalyptic summoning of Ragnaros the Firelord. Today, the gorge is heavily worked by the Dark Iron clan, whose extensive slave mines in the Cauldron are closely monitored by the breakaway Thorium Brotherhood. Before the War of the Three Hammers, the territory that is now Searing Gorge was a green, rolling mountain region connected to the Redridge chain. That lush landscape ceased to exist over two hundred and thirty years ago when Sorcerer-Thane Thaurissan, desperate to turn the tide of defeat, summoned Ragnaros from the depths beneath the world. The cataclysmic emergence of the Firelord tore the earth asunder, raised Blackrock Mountain, reduced the grand Dark Iron city of Thaurissan to smoking ruins, and burned the northern valley into a cracked expanse of ash, sulfur, and volcanic glass. Seeking raw materials to supply their war machine after the loss of their old capital, the Dark Iron dwarves seized the desolate gorge. In the center of the valley lies the Cauldron, a colossal open-pit excavation plunging deep into the stone. Within its lower recesses sits the Slag Pit, a brutal subterranean mining complex. Here, Dark Iron overseers and lumbering war golems drive captured enemies into grueling slave labor, pulling iron, mithril, and rare deposits of Dark Iron ore out of the burning rock under the constant threat of lava surges and roaming beasts. Perched on the northern crags overlooking the excavation sits Thorium Point, the fortified outpost of the Thorium Brotherhood. Having split from their kin in Blackrock Mountain, these master craftsmen offer neutral shelter to travelers willing to undermine the Dark Iron operations or supply them with rare smelting components. Access to the gorge itself is tightly restricted: the Alliance keeps the Stonewrought Pass locked down behind heavy iron gates toward Loch Modan, while Horde expeditions from nearby Kargath have cut a narrow trail through the eastern badlands to scout the region.

zone:shadowfang.text: Shadowfang Keep. Perched on the rugged bluffs above Pyrewood Village, Shadowfang Keep is the gloomy stronghold of the rogue Kirin Tor wizard, Archmage Arugal. Once the ancestral estate of Baron Silverlaine, the bastion now teems with feral worgen beasts and the tormented phantoms of its slaughtered defenders. For adventurers traversing southern Silverpine, the keep represents the dark epicenter of the beastly scourge consuming the region. Before it was shrouded in nightmare, Shadowfang was known as Silverlaine Keep, a noble seat garrisoned by the pious Commander Springvale. When the Scourge swept through Lordaeron during the Third War, Dalaran's wizards fell in droves. Desperate to stem the rising dead, Archmage Arugal defied Kirin Tor leadership and delved into the research of the wizard Ur, summoning extra-dimensional worgen to turn the tide. The summoned beasts savaged the undead, but rapidly slipped beyond all mortal control, breaking into southern Silverpine and storming the bastion. Baron Silverlaine and his entire court were massacred, doomed to haunt the stone halls alongside the feral monsters that overran their home. Broken by guilt and madness, Arugal retreated within the blood-stained battlements, adopting the ravenous wolf-men as his beloved 'children' and christening the castle Shadowfang Keep. Deep in the stone roosts, lupine packs and shadowy hounds flourish under trainers like Wolf Master Nandos, watched over by Arugal's massive lupine beast, Fenrus the Devourer. Outside the walls, the curse did not halt; nearby Pyrewood Village remains trapped in a horrifying nocturnal cycle, its residents walking as men by day and hunting as ravenous worgen beneath the moon, tethered inexorably to the mad archmage perched on the heights above.

zone:shendralas.text: Shen'dralas. Shen'dralas is a rugged, contested wilderness situated between Feralas, Mulgore, and south-eastern Desolace. Dominated by ancient night elven remnants and troubled borders, it serves as a volatile crossroads where encroaching centaur, displaced outcasts, and bristling quilboar collide. Tucked away in the heights south-east of Desolace and bordered by Mulgore and Feralas, Shen'dralas is a raw borderland far removed from major faction capitols. Its craggy passes and hidden enclaves harbor desperate groups carving out existence on the edge of wild Kalimdor. From secluded vantage points like Evenshade Overlook to lawless refuges like Outcast Hideaway, the zone is defined by those who wish to watch unseen or stay forgotten. The land bears the distinct mark of the highborne legacy that gave it its name, yet it is far from peaceful. Centaur conflict bleeds across the Magram Front, keeping old blood feuds alive and well along its borders. Meanwhile, encroaching quilboar maintain fortified redoubts such as Bristleback Retreat, turning every shadowed ravine into contested territory for any traveler passing through. Leading out north-west toward Desolace lies the Valley of Bones, a grim corridor that serves as the primary overland access route into Shen'dralas. Bleached by sun and wind, this passage stands as a harsh reminder of the violent struggles that constantly ripple through these crags.

zone:silithus.text: Silithus. Silithus is a desolate, wind-scoured desert located in the far southwestern corner of Kalimdor. Beneath its arid sands lie vast colonies of insectoid silithid and the ancient ruins of Ahn'Qiraj, sealed a millennium ago behind the formidable Scarab Wall. Today, the druids of the Cenarion Circle maintain an embattled vigil against creeping swarms, doomsday cultists. Reaching Silithus requires navigating through the primeval jungle of Un'Goro Crater and ascending a wide, rocky pass nestled in its northwestern corner. The transition is stark: lush primordial growth vanishes into a vast expanse of shifting dunes, jagged stone, and unnatural towering hives. Water is virtually nonexistent, and the winds carry the hum of insect wings and the whispering sands. The Cenarion Circle maintains Cenarion Hold near the center of the desert, serving as the sole bastion of civilization and shelter for travelers, researchers, and warriors braving the hostile wastes. A thousand years ago, this arid expanse served as the battlefield for the War of the Shifting Sands. An allied army of night elves and great dragonflights fought desperately to drive back the Qiraji, an insidious insectoid empire spawned from the ancient Aqiri civilization. When total victory proved impossible, the defenders sealed the swarms within their stronghold using the Scarab Wall and the enchanted Scarab Dais. While the monumental gates held, subterranean tunnels allowed the beast-like silithids to burrow out, establishing sprawling colonies such as Hive'Ashi, Hive'Zora, and Hive'Regal throughout the sands. The apocalyptic Twilight's Hammer cult has entrenched itself across several fortified outposts, summoning elemental terrors and venerating the dark power slumbering beneath Ahn'Qiraj. Cenarion Circle observers monitor the desert's spreading silithid colonies and the ancient threat behind the Scarab Wall.

zone:silverpine.text: Silverpine Forest. Silverpine Forest is an eerie, mist-laden woodland stretching along Lordaeron's western coast between Tirisfal Glades and the sealed Greymane Wall. Haunted by the lingering scars of the Scourge plague, it serves as the contested southern frontier of the Forsaken. Travelers here face feral worgen roaming the shadows, diseased gnolls, and hostile human enclaves. Once celebrated as a lush wonder of Lordaeron through which noble travelers journeyed to Capital City, Silverpine Forest has withered under the touch of the Third War. Ghostly fogs weave between dying, silver-barked pines, and ruined farmsteads sit abandoned to the wilderness. To the north lies Tirisfal Glades, while the eastern shore borders Lordamere Lake. To the south stands the imposing and shut Greymane Wall, sealing off the isolationist kingdom of Gilneas from the surrounding chaos. The Forsaken maintain their central outpost at the Sepulcher, striving to secure the woods from enemies on all sides. Silverpine's most infamous peril is the worgen curse. High above the southwest woods sits Shadowfang Keep, the former seat of Baron Silverlaine, now dominated by the mad Dalaran archmage Arugal. Seeking to repel the Scourge during the Third War, Arugal summoned extra-dimensional wolf-beasts. The creatures turned on their summoners, spreading a lycanthropic curse across the southern woods. In Pyrewood Village, ordinary-looking human villagers go about their chores by daylight, but transform into savage worgen beneath the night sky.

zone:stonetalon.text: Stonetalon Mountains. The Stonetalon Mountains are a rugged, wind-carved chain of craggy peaks bordering Ashenvale, the Barrens, and Desolace. Revered by both the night elves and the tauren as a sacred sanctuary, the region's sacred heights stand in sharp contrast to the smoke and machinery choking its lower canyons. Today, the mountains are torn by deforestation, volatile elemental devastation, and simmering border hostilities. Rising sharply out of central Kalimdor, the Stonetalon range catches the moisture drifting from the western seas, giving birth to sudden downpours and treacherous, rain-slick sandstone trails. The dominant feature of the lower valleys is the incessant scouring gale known as the Ill Winds, capable of blinding travelers with grit or throwing the careless straight off sheer cliffsides. Higher up, evergreen forests mantle the ridges surrounding Stonetalon Peak, where the night elves tend ancestral barrows and glades, watching over the sacred roosts of wyverns and hippogryphs that nest along Mirkfallon Lake. The peaceful solitude of the range has been violently disrupted by the arrival of the Venture Company. Setting up sprawling logging camps and digging deep strip mines in Windshear Crag, the goblins—aided by the deranged leper gnome Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle—have clear-cut old-growth timber, blackened the skies with furnace smoke, and poured industrial sludge into the mountain runoff. Their greed has provoked swift retaliation: local shamans from Orgrimmar answered the agonized cries of the mountain spirits, while small Alliance camps stationed nearby fight back against the defilers to protect what remains of the highlands. To the south lies the Charred Vale, once a blossoming wilderness, now reduced to an ash-covered wasteland churning with rogue fire elementals, black dragonspawn, and harpies. While the peaks were the historic site where the Horde and Alliance forged an uneasy truce during the Third War under the guidance of the mysterious Oracle, current relations are fraying. Renegade Grimtotem tauren operate out of seized encampments, and Darkspear trolls in Malaka'jin clash with Alliance incursions pushing outward from the Barrens and Ashenvale.

zone:swampofsorrows.text: Swamp of Sorrows. The Swamp of Sorrows is a murky, brackish wetland tucked between Deadwind Pass and the arid Blasted Lands. Once the northern expanse of the ancient Black Morass, its salt-crusted bogs are home to dangerous wildlife, green dragonspawn, and the ruined Temple of Atal'Hakkar sunken beneath the Pool of Tears. While the Horde maintains the fortified garrison of Stonard, the Alliance has no safe haven within the mire, leaving the wilderness largely untamed. Long before the coming of the Orcish Horde, these marshes formed the northern half of an enormous wetlands known as the Black Morass. Following the shattering of the Gurubashi Empire, the fanatical Atal'ai trolls fled into the mire to erect the Temple of Atal'Hakkar, intending to summon their bloodthirsty loa, Hakkar the Soulflayer. Sensing the catastrophe, the Aspect Ysera unleashed her powers, drowning the cursed pyramid beneath the waters of the Pool of Tears. Green dragonflight guardians led by Eranikus were stationed to vigilantly watch over the drowned structure. When the Dark Portal's cataclysm later scorched the southern morass into the Blasted Lands, this northern fen earned its current sorrowful name. Stonard serves as the primary civilized foothold in the swamp. Originally established during the First War alongside the now-ruined settlements of Rockard and Kyross, the outpost was rebuilt under Thrall to serve as the Horde's southernmost staging ground in the Eastern Kingdoms. Beyond Stonard's palisades, strange wanderers roam the fen. A group of draenei stragglers stranded on Azeroth succumbed to homesickness and madness, degenerating into feral Lost Ones. However, a small enclave of lucid Broken exiles persists at the Harborage, wary but willing to trade peacefully with travelers. Surviving the swamp requires constant vigilance against its predatory wildlife. Deep bogs hide lunging crocolisks, venomous spiders, prowling swamp jaguars, and wandering bog beasts encrusted with marsh debris. Coastal caverns and the Misty Reed Strand crawl with vicious murlocs, while the salt-laden tide creeps continually inland, preserving rotten logs in thick briny crusts. Farther east lies Sorrowmurk, where aggressive elite dragonspawn fiercely guard the approaches to the Sunken Temple, attacking anyone who strays near their vigil.

zone:teldrassil.text: Teldrassil. Teldrassil, meaning 'Crown of the Earth', is a gargantuan new World Tree raised off Kalimdor's northwest coast. Grown by the druids in the wake of the Third War, its colossal boughs support an entire twilit wilderness and the night elf capital of Darnassus. Yet beneath its tranquil, moonlit canopy, a creeping corruption has begun to stir. Teldrassil is not merely a tree; it is an elevated ecosystem standing tall amidst the waters of the Veiled Sea. Its gargantuan limbs support rolling hills, flowing rivers fed by morning dew, misty lakes, and dense ancient glades. At its western edge sits Darnassus, the grand capital of the kaldorei. At the base of its monumental trunk lies Rut'theran Village, connected to the crown above by a mystical gateway and serving as the island's primary harbor. Following the sacrifice of Nordrassil during the Third War and the mysterious disappearance of Shan'do Malfurion Stormrage into the Emerald Dream, Archdruid Fandral Staghelm convinced the Circle of Ancients to grow a replacement. Staghelm hoped to restore the kaldorei to their lost immortality. However, Nozdormu and the Dragon Aspects deemed the effort hubristic and withheld their blessings. Without their vital warding, Teldrassil's growth has suffered from unnatural flaws.

zone:thousandneedles.text: Thousand Needles. Thousand Needles is a sprawling canyon of sheer sandstone pillars and sunbaked salt pans in southern Kalimdor. Tauren tribes cling to settlements atop towering mesas to escape aggressive centaur packs, while gnomish and goblin tinkerers run high-speed rocket cars across the dried-up seabed of the Shimmering Flats. Before the Great Sundering shattered ancient Kalimdor, this territory was a lush river canyon fed by inland waterways flowing out toward the sea. The cataclysm tore the continent apart, thrusting the riverbed above the water table and altering the river's path until only dry stone and sandstone spires remained. Today, dozens of slender cylindrical columns rise from the canyon floor like a petrified forest. Tauren settled on the summits, stringing precarious rope bridges between peaks to establish villages out of reach of the hostile centaur marauders patrolling the shadow-draped canyon floor below. Atop the needle-like spires, life is far from peaceful. At Freewind Post, tauren loyal to the Horde contend not only with predatory wind serpents and wyverns from Highperch, but also with their treacherous kin: the militant Grimtotem clan entrenched at Darkcloud Pinnacle. Cliffwatcher Longhorn oversees the defense of the plateau, seeking bold fighters to strike at Grimtotem agitators and secure the fragile bridges linking the peaks. To the north, the enormous mechanical winches of the Great Lift carry travelers down from the southern Barrens, though crossing the canyon floor remains a deadly gambit. To the southeast, the canyon walls peel back into the Shimmering Flats, an enormous, desiccated salt pan sitting below sea level. In this harsh, blinding white expanse, gnomes and goblins maintain an uneasy neutrality around the Mirage Raceway. Rival engineers Pozzik and Fizzle Brassbolts race experimental rocket cars across the hard salt to settle which race possesses technological superiority. The pit stop attracts scoundrels, swindlers like Kravel Koalbeard, and hunters hunting the hardy scorpions, turtles, and basilisks that roam the searing basin.

zone:thunderbluff.text: Thunder Bluff. Thunder Bluff is the magnificent capital city of the tauren, perched atop windswept red-rock mesas rising above the grasslands of Mulgore. Founded by High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof after uniting the nomadic tribes with the aid of the New Horde, it serves as the cultural, spiritual, and mercantile heart of his people. Connected by swaying rope bridges and wooden lifts, the city offers safety from centaur marauders and a peaceful sanctuary for travelers across Kalimdor. For countless generations, the tauren lived as nomadic wanderers across Kalimdor, locked in a brutal struggle for survival against ravenous centaur tribes. That desperate era ended during the Third War when Cairne Bloodhoof joined forces with Warchief Thrall. Together, the orcs and tauren broke the centaur assaults and secured the lush pastures of Mulgore. To protect their future, Cairne led the allied tribes to the safety of these natural stone bastions, founding Thunder Bluff as the first unified, permanent home the tauren had possessed in centuries. Spanning several high mesas linked by suspended rope bridges, Thunder Bluff seamlessly blends natural architecture with tauren practicality. The central bluffs host the bustling markets, bank, inn, and towering Wind Rider roost, while three specialized mesas branch out across the abyss. Hunter Rise serves the city's scouts and trackers; Elder Rise hosts lorekeepers and the Cenarion Circle under Archdruid Hamuul Runetotem; and Spirit Rise is devoted to spiritual communion, sheltering shamans, priests, and the mysterious subterranean caverns known as the Pools of Vision.

zone:tirisfal.text: Tirisfal Glades. Tirisfal Glades is the haunting northern territory of Lordaeron, now serving as the heartland of Lady Sylvanas Windrunner and the Forsaken. Beneath blighted skies and rotting boughs lie fallen manors, dormant crypts, and the vast underground capital of the Undercity. Surrounded by mindless Scourge and zealous Scarlet crusaders, it is a perilous realm where free-willed undead carve out their survival. Once the fertile cradle of humanity, Tirisfal Glades has withered beneath the curse of the Lich King's plague. The sun rarely penetrates the murky gloom, casting an eternal sickly pale over dying woods, neglected pumpkin patches, and cold coastal hills. While remnants of old farmsteads like the Agamand Mills and Balnir Farmstead remain, their former masters have largely been swept into mass graves or risen as restless dead. Despite the devastation, a dark resilience permeates the countryside, anchored by towns like Brill and the cloistered sanctuary of Deathknell, where freshly awakened Forsaken learn to endure their second life. Though Lady Sylvanas claims dominion over the region from the subterranean Ruins of Lordaeron, the Forsaken remain embattled on all sides. Residual Scourge thralls still infest hollows, fields, and dilapidated crypts, entirely subservient to the frozen throne of Northrend. To the east, the fanatical Scarlet Crusade has made northern Tirisfal its primary bastion, operating out of the Scarlet Monastery. Zealously devoted to the extermination of every undead creature, living and unliving alike, their outposts and patrols wage constant guerrilla warfare against Forsaken scouts and civilian travelers. Long before human kingdoms crowned their first monarchs, the Glades bore an ancient legacy. High elven exiles briefly tried to settle these woods before shadowy energies deep beneath the earth began driving them mad, prompting their migration north. In later centuries, the secret mortal cabal known as the Council of Tirisfal chose these shadowed groves to empower solitary Guardians, shielding Azeroth from demonic intrusion.

zone:undercity.text: Undercity. Deep beneath the shattered ruins of Lordaeron's Capital City lies the Undercity, the dark stronghold of the Forsaken. Originally carved out of ancient royal crypts and dungeons by the Scourge, it was seized by Lady Sylvanas Windrunner and remade into an impenetrable subterranean sanctuary. Today it serves as the seat of Forsaken power and the Horde's vital bastion in the northern Eastern Kingdoms. Long before the plague swept Lordaeron, the catacombs, dungeons, and sewers beneath the palace were collectively known as the Undercity. It held the tombs of nobility, the kingdom's deepest prisons—where the former Warchief Orgrim Doomhammer was once held before his escape—and the poorest denizens of the realm. When Arthas Menethil murdered King Terenas and laid waste to the capital in 20 ADP, the prince ordered his undead servants to excavate and expand the subterranean passages into a fortified seat of Scourge rule. The Scourge never saw their dark capital completed. When the Lich King's powers waned following the battle of Mount Hyjal, Lady Sylvanas Windrunner broke free from the hive mind, taking thousands of undead with her. She lured Arthas into an ambush and drove him back to Northrend. After a vicious three-way civil war against Scourge remnants, dreadlords, and human resistance, Sylvanas claimed the half-finished catacombs. Naming her people the Forsaken, she oversaw years of labor completing the sprawling subterranean city. The Undercity is laid out in concentric rings divided into functional quarters. At its heart lies the Trade Quarter, connected by great lifts to the palace ruins above. Surrounding it are the War Quarter, Rogues' Quarter, Magic Quarter, and the toxic Apothecarium, where the Royal Apothecary Society brews virulent plagues in green slime-filled canals. Deeper still lies the Royal Quarter, where the Banshee Queen holds court alongside her dreadlord commander, Varimathras, guarded by legions of towering abominations.

zone:ungoro.text: Un'Goro Crater. Un'Goro Crater is a sunken, primordial jungle tucked between the arid wastes of Tanaris and Silithus. Dominated by roaming dinosaurs, living elementals, and a central volcano, this lush caldera is filled with ancient Titan relics and power crystals whose origins remain a profound mystery. Sandwiched between desert expanses, Un'Goro Crater defies the geography of southern Kalimdor. Ancient night elf records detailing the War of the Shifting Sands note that the insectoid Qiraji were turned back at the crater's edges, unable to penetrate what their tongue named the 'God Lands.' Scholars theorize the caldera served as a testing ground or ancient dwelling for the Titans during the shaping of Kalimdor. Stone pylons rise along the ridges, humming with energy, while crystal formations of blue, red, green, and yellow sprout through the primeval earth. Un'Goro contains no cities, towns, or native humanoid societies. Instead, life thrives in an untamed, primeval state. Apex devilsaurs stalk the flats of Terror Run, predatory bloodpetals lash out in the marshlands, and oozes creep across the tar pits of Lakkari. At the heart of the crater looms Fire Plume Ridge, an active volcanic peak teeming with hostile fire elementals led by the entity Blazerunner. For explorers and skinners, the basin offers unmatched natural wealth—including the coveted hides of devilsaurs—provided one survives the food chain. Civilized presence in the crater is limited almost entirely to Marshal's Refuge, an elevated camp tucked into the northern cliffs. Led by Williden Marshal, an expedition of scientists, naturalists, and fortune seekers attempted to catalogue the basin's treasures only to be battered by the monstrous wildlife and driven to high ground. Today, the refuge serves as an embattled staging ground for intrepid travelers studying the crater's mysterious power crystals, mapping volcanic activity, and keeping a watchful eye on encroaching silithid swarms breaching the southern ridges.

zone:wailing.text: Wailing Caverns. Tucked beneath the Lushwater Oasis in the arid Barrens lies the Wailing Caverns, a labyrinthine system of subterranean springs and fissures named for the eerie whistling of trapped steam. What began as a noble druidic effort to revitalize Kalimdor's sun-bleached savanna has devolved into a warped, poisonous underworld. The caverns now teem with twisted wildlife and fallen disciples corrupted by a deep, unnatural nightmare. The night elf druid Naralex originally discovered this vast water system and devised an ambitious design: by opening a conduit straight into the Emerald Dream, he would siphon pure primal life essence through the subterranean springs, transforming the parched Barrens back into a thriving, verdant paradise. Deep within the caverns, Naralex slipped into communion with the Dream, anchored by his loyal acolytes. Tragically, rather than tapping into pure vitality, the druid's sleeping mind touched the Emerald Nightmare. The festering corruption instantly seized him, transforming his well-intentioned conduit into a valve pouring venom and madness into the underground waterways. As the Nightmare's dark energy radiated from Naralex's helpless form, his students succumbed to the madness. Forsaking the tranquil wisdom of the Cenarion Circle, they formed the fanatical Druids of the Fang. Taking reptilian forms, the sect's leaders—Lady Anacondra, Lord Cobrahn, Lord Pythas, and Lord Serpentis—now embrace the venomous mutation of the caverns rather than fighting it. They actively shield their sleeping master from any outside interference, believing this twisted growth is the true evolution of nature.

zone:westernplaguelands.text: Western Plaguelands. Once the fertile agricultural breadbasket of northern Lordaeron, the Western Plaguelands now choke beneath a toxic mist and legions of undead. While Kel'Thuzad's cauldrons ruined the region's farms and towns, the soil still clings tenaciously to life. The Argent Dawn, the Alliance, the Forsaken, and the Scarlet Crusade all wage desperate campaigns across its blighted fields. Before the Third War, this land was a verdant corridor of farms stretching east from Tirisfal Glades toward Darrowmere Lake. Hearthglen governed the northern administration from Mardenholde Keep, while the sprawling town of Andorhal orchestrated the storage and export of grain across the kingdom. That crucial agricultural role made the region Kel'Thuzad's primary target. By introducing the Plague of Undeath directly into the grain shipments at Andorhal, the Cult of the Damned turned Lordaeron's sustenance into its doom. To permanently poison the soil, the Scourge raised four massive plague cauldrons across the largest agricultural estates: Felstone Field, Dalson's Tears, the Writhing Haunt, and Gahrron's Withering. Today, monstrous Cauldron Lords maintain these noxious vats, pumping venomous fog into the atmosphere. The surrounding trees twist with swollen, tumorous growths, and blighted wildlife rampages through the brush. Beneath Caer Darrow on Darrowmere Lake, Darkmaster Gandling trains necromancers within Scholomance, compounding the undead threat. Despite the omnipresence of the Scourge, several factions maintain embattled footholds. The Scarlet Crusade controls the fortress of Hearthglen in the north, purging anything they deem tainted with rabid zeal. To the south, Alliance forces stage from Chillwind Camp, while the Forsaken defend their borders at the Bulwark. Mediating and directing the fight against the undead cauldrons is the neutral Argent Dawn, which aids champions of both factions and guards Uther's Tomb—the last truly sanctified ground in the region.

zone:westfall.text: Westfall. Once the fertile breadbasket of the Kingdom of Stormwind, Westfall has collapsed into a windswept, neglected territory overrun by outlaws. Deprived of official crown support and military garrisons, its surviving homesteaders cling to their farms while the Defias Brotherhood tightens its grip from the abandoned mining town of Moonbrook. For generations, Westfall fed the Kingdom of Stormwind. Its rolling pastures and wheat fields flourished until the aftermath of the Second War brought financial exhaustion and political neglect. When the kingdom poured its resources elsewhere and failed to maintain its garrisons, the territory grew fallow. Today, barren pastures, howling coastal gusts, rogue harvest golems, and raiding Riverpaw gnolls make daily survival a constant trial for the stubborn few who refuse to abandon their homesteads. Westfall's collapse accelerated when the Stonemasons Guild, denied payment for rebuilding Stormwind City, turned to open revolt. Outlawed and exiled under Edwin VanCleef, the stonemasons reconstituted themselves as the Defias Brotherhood. They claimed Westfall as their stronghold, burning stubborn farmers' fields, salting soil, and seizing abandoned mines. Operating out of the ghost town of Moonbrook, the Brotherhood now rules the majority of the countryside in all but name. With the House of Nobles ignoring Westfall's plight, local inhabitants took up their own defense. Based at the fortified post of Sentinel Hill, Gryan Stoutmantle organized the People's Militia—a volunteer force attempting to hold the line against gnolls and bandits. Lacking formal soldiers and supplies from Stormwind, the Militia relies on wandering adventurers to push back the Defias tide and protect the remaining farms.

zone:zephras.text: Zephras Isle. Zephras Isle is a flying island suspended within Skywall, the Elemental Plane of air. It serves as the ancestral starting home of the Skyborne, whose society now faces an existential crisis as the island's sustaining magic steadily erodes. With contact severed from neighboring sky-realms, its inhabitants struggle against elemental collapse and arriving refugees. Zephras Isle is an isolated landmass adrift in the endless winds of Skywall. For generations, the Skyborne lived here alongside native air elementals who helped preserve the magical currents holding the isle aloft. However, several centuries ago, those elemental stewards vanished entirely. Deprived of their presence and guardianship, the latent enchantments upholding the land have slowly begun to fail, causing Zephras to slowly fracture and destabilize. Zephras was not the only sanctuary inhabited by the Skyborne within the Elemental Plane. Sister islands known as Anvilas and Siroccas also drifted across Skywall, but communications between them ceased after the elementals vanished. In recent times, refugees from these crumbling neighboring landmasses have managed to reach Zephras seeking safety, bearing grim tidings that the other islands are disintegrating outright beneath their feet. With their own landmass in slow decay, the Skyborne of Zephras have begun looking beyond the boundaries of Skywall toward Azeroth. From the skydocks of Valanaar, airships now venture forth to establish rare lifelines to the mortal realm. These voyages connect the airy domain directly to points on Azeroth, including the outskirts of Dalaran in the Alterac Mountains and the Skywatcher Plateau in Mulgore.
